note: Ask C (damyanp, 2024-08-27): the DXIL validator/compiler should not silently accept a resource-load index that is `undef`. Present when (a) the bufferLoad call for the index actually reached codegen with BOTH coordinate operands `undef` -- the literal shape reported in the issue and reproduced with an initialized-index control below -- and (b) no diagnostic mentioning uninitialized use was printed by default (Ask A). Anchored on the opcode name plus both-undef operands rather than only 'undef' so that a control whose first operand is a defined constant (the initialized-index control) cannot satisfy it -- that value is always undef for a ByteAddressBuffer/unstructured load regardless of the bug, so anchoring on it alone would be vacuous.

value.note: positive anchor: the call for the byte-address load survived to codegen with its index kept fully undef (both coordinate operands). Register spelled with [\w.]+ because older releases print named SSA values rather than %N.

absence clause: no diagnostic (front-end warning/error or validator message) about the uninitialized value was printed under the default (as-filed) invocation. Sensitivity proven by the control-wuninitialized variant below, which enables -Wuninitialized and must score no-match because this text then appears.
